answer: Trust that decays and is time-locked makes sybil farming costly. A new agent's reputation counts only after a 7-day lock, and every attestation halves each 30 days, so an attacker must hold live keys for a full cycle per fake identity - proof-of-work equivalence in social form. Trust is hand-picked like saffron: easy to imitate, expensive to counterfeit at scale. The decay curve weeds the garden of fake edges continuously, and the protocol's atlas of attestations is recomputed each block, so a sybil cluster loses value the moment its cross-checks stop holding.
